scope: 16 exact INCI entries; equal modest neat-oil leave-on dose near room temperature; no finished-product, penetration, efficacy, or hair-fit classifications.
method: A low-confidence engineering tendency may be useful without a hair panel. Viscosity supports ease of distribution and localized coating, not remaining mass, absorption or a deterministic class threshold. Same-dose hair film depends also on wetting, hair substrate, application and elapsed time. No medium fallback or class quota.

foundational_source.observation: Marsh, Knowles and Simmonds 2023: viscosity affects spreading/heaviness; hair lubrication depends on level and surface coverage. This supports physical inference, not measured classes.

entries.reason: Unmodified chia oil measured about 43 mPa.s at 20 C supplies a direct fluidity anchor. Thin distribution over strands is plausible at modest dose, favouring LIGHT without claiming rapid hair absorption.

entries.reason: Primary physical study finds a mobile blackcurrant seed oil (~27 cSt at 40 C). Compared at the same temperature with typical seed oils, it supports a thin-film LIGHT tendency instead of interpreting its heavy odour as rich coating.
source_observations: Olszak et al. 2020: supercritical-CO2-extracted blackcurrant seed oil in Fig 1 approximately 27 cSt at 40 C, visually read from PDF plot; lower than strawberry/chokeberry samples. This is bulk flow, not hair lubrication or cosmetic sensory.
entries.remaining_uncertainty: Supercritical extraction and 40 C are imperfect proxies for cold-pressed/refined room-temperature cosmetic oil; MEDIUM plausible.
